claims.text: In HEAs outside Nb-Ta and Ti-rich matrices, superconducting transition temperature is primarily governed by valence electron concentration.
In these HEAs, superconducting transition temperature is primarily governed by the degree of chemical disorder.
Valence electron concentration and chemical disorder modulate the density of states at the Fermi level.
Valence electron concentration and chemical disorder modulate electron-phonon coupling strength.
HEAs with a near-optimal VEC and moderate disorder while retaining a single-phase solid solution will exhibit higher Tc.
Excessive chemical disorder suppresses superconductivity.
Deviation from the optimal VEC suppresses superconductivity.
Changing alloy composition can systematically adjust average VEC and chemical disorder while preserving a single-phase solid solution.
VEC determines the density of states at the Fermi level.
The density of states at the Fermi level influences electron-phonon coupling and thereby Tc.
Chemical disorder affects electronic scattering.
Chemical disorder can enhance or suppress superconductivity through effects on electron mobility and phonon modes.
A VEC of approximately 5-7 is near the optimal range for conventional superconductors relevant to the proposed HEAs.
HEAs with VEC approximately 5-7 and moderate disorder will show measurable superconducting transitions.
Such HEAs will have Tc comparable to or slightly below ordered alloys with similar VEC.
Alloys with excessive disorder or VEC far from the proposed optimum will exhibit suppressed or absent superconductivity.
The proposed baseline HEA with nonoptimal VEC and/or excessive disorder is expected to show no superconducting transition above 2 K.
There is a lack of direct experimental evidence for superconductivity in HEAs outside Nb-Ta and Ti-rich systems.
The hypothesis is restricted to single-phase solid solutions containing at least five elements at 5 atomic percent or more each, excluding Nb-Ta-dominated, Ti-rich, and strongly magnetic systems.
Failure of near-optimal-VEC, moderately disordered HEAs to superconduct above 2 K, or absence of the predicted Tc correlation with VEC and disorder, would falsify the hypothesis.
